note: Four cups beside the basket. Two keep a published recipe's own quantities; two are composed from the records' cited descriptions and say so. Everything scales off the finished cup.
house_note: Buffalo serves blue cheese and America buys ranch, by a distance. Both are cold, both are mostly fat, and both exist to put out a fire the sauce started. Make either one the day before — the garlic and the pepper need the night.

kinds.name: Blue cheese
kinds.region: Buffalo, and the plate the wing arrived on
kinds.says: Chunky, cold, and not negotiable in western New York.

anchor.title: Cookbook:Blue Cheese Dressing
anchor.note: The recipe's own quantities, scaled to the cup. Wikibooks notes it is adapted from its own buttermilk ranch.

steps: Whisk everything except the cheese until it is smooth.
Dice the cheese into half-inch cubes; the crumbs are meant to be there.
Fold the cubes and crumbs through. Chill it.
Keep it thick. A thin blue cheese runs off a wing and lands on your shirt.

kinds.name: Buttermilk ranch
kinds.region: everywhere, and outselling blue cheese nationally
kinds.says: Buttermilk, mayonnaise, sour cream, herbs. Tangy without being sweet.

anchor.title: Cookbook:Buttermilk Ranch Dressing
anchor.note: The recipe's own quantities, scaled to the cup. Hidden Valley's formula is a trade secret and nothing here claims to be it.

steps: Mix until smooth, as the recipe says.
Rest it overnight. Fresh ranch tastes of raw garlic and little else.
Thin it with more buttermilk if you want it pourable.

kinds.name: Hot wing dip
kinds.says: Blue cheese and sour cream with cayenne stirred straight in. Not a cooling dip.

anchor.title: Cookbook:Hot Wing Dip
anchor.note: The recipe's own quantities, scaled to the cup. It is written to be served WITH wings and celery, not instead of them.

steps: Combine the cheese, cayenne, sour cream, garlic and salt in a serving bowl.
Two tablespoons of cayenne to a cup is what the recipe says. Start at half if that reads high to you.

kinds.name: Alabama white
kinds.says: A dip you can also cook with, though it splits over heat.

anchor.note: Composed from the sauce record's cited description — mayonnaise, vinegar, black pepper, lemon, sometimes horseradish. Big Bob Gibson's own formula is unpublished and nothing here claims to be it.

steps: Whisk it cold. It should pour.
Overnight is better than an hour.
Dunk smoked wings straight into it, or keep it in a cup beside them.
